Also important to note we are technically in a blackout period for equities at the moment (share buybacks are halted)

As evidenced in Saylor's latest acquisition that went from billions down to a measly 100 mill clip

He's temporarily run out of ammo and he is the marginal spot buyer in market (which is great but obviously comes with its own idiosyncratic risks)

Broad market is also digesting inflation fears etc. so all this lends to a short term temper tantrum and a window of weakness 

So simply vibe around the noise. Will get more upside no doubt, just trying to give a bit of context for why the ride is unlikely to be as smooth as is often perceived

Unfortunate but that's just how the cookie crumbles

So looks like more downward chop/ranging is likely coming so set those alerts for lower and get ready to eat some volatility
